concepts.def: Internal framework of 206 bones providing support, movement, protection and blood-cell production.
Skull, vertebral column, ribs and sternum; protects vital organs.
Bones of arms, legs, shoulder and pelvic girdles; enables movement.
Where two or more bones meet; classified by type and movement.
Freely movable joint with synovial fluid; e.g., hinge (elbow), ball-and-socket (hip).
Tough connective tissue joining bone to bone, stabilising joints.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Performance in Physical Education (NEA) — a core area of GCSE PE.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Performance in Physical Education (NEA) brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Performance in Physical Education (NEA).

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.
